technical_and_design_decisions: For the Reactor 2.0.4 upgrade (U1), Maven dependency management will be used to pin the Reactor version across all Spring XD submodules, with priority given to maintaining backward compatibility with existing user code.

For the Ambari HA XD-Admin setup (U2), leader election for XD-Admin instances will be implemented using Apache Zookeeper (an existing Spring XD dependency), and a shared network file system will be used for cross-instance cluster state persistence.

For the @EnableModule annotation model (U3), Spring's @Import and @Conditional annotations will be used for auto-configuration, with @Input/@Output supporting both method-level and field-level bean definition for flexibility, while maintaining full backward compatibility with existing explicit channel bean definitions.
For the Kryo optimization work (U4), the existing Spring Integration Kryo codec implementation will be reused to minimize new code and reduce risk of introducing bugs.
For the 1.2.x branch EC2 CI migration (U5), existing project AWS infrastructure templates and IAM roles will be reused, and S3 will be used for storing test reports and build artifacts.

For the Maven repo module installation feature (U6), the Maven Aether library (already used in the Spring ecosystem) will be used for artifact resolution, and the CLI command will follow existing Spring XD CLI design patterns for consistency.

For the serialization codec move to Spring Integration (U7), the existing public API of the codec will be preserved to avoid breaking changes for Spring XD users, and the codec will be added to the Spring Integration core module for maximum reusability.

For the CloudController XD Admin SPI (U8), the implementation will be based on the existing spike deliverables (XD-3194/XD-3229) to reduce rework, and will align with existing spring-cloud-data module deployer interfaces for consistency with other deployment targets.
assumptions: All required access to AWS (for EC2 provisioning and S3 storage), Apache Ambari, test Maven repositories, and Cloud Foundry test environments is pre-provisioned and available for development and testing without additional approval processes.
The existing Spring XD 1.2.x test suite is fully functional and can be executed on the new EC2 infrastructure without requiring changes to test code.
The spike deliverables referenced in U8 (XD-3194 and XD-3229) are complete, accessible to the development team, and contain accurate implementation guidance for the CloudController SPI.
No breaking changes to existing public APIs of Spring XD, Spring Integration, or Spring Cloud Data are required to implement any of the user stories in this increment.
All required code repositories (Spring XD, Spring Integration, spring-cloud-data, spring-cloud-stream) have appropriate access permissions configured for the development team.
The Reactor 2.0.4 release is fully compatible with Java 17, which is required for the Spring Framework versions used in the project.

activities.activity_description: Update all Maven pom.xml files in the Spring XD codebase to reference Reactor 2.0.4, resolve any transitive dependency conflicts, and confirm local build success.
Execute the full existing Spring XD test suite against the Reactor 2.0.4 upgrade to identify all compatibility issues and failing tests.
Fix all identified compatibility issues between Spring XD components and Reactor 2.0.4, re-run failing tests to confirm fixes, and update any relevant upgrade documentation.
Design the Ambari service definition changes to support deploying multiple XD-Admin instances, including leader election configuration, shared storage setup, and load balancing configuration.
Update the Ambari service definition scripts, configuration templates, and metadata to support deploying and managing multiple XD-Admin instances for high availability.
Deploy the updated Ambari service in a test environment, validate that multiple XD-Admin instances start correctly, fail over properly, and handle client requests as expected.

Design the structure and behavior of the @EnableModule, @Input, and @Output annotations, including how they integrate with Spring's application context to auto-register channel beans and adapters, while maintaining backward compatibility with existing module definitions.

Implement the @EnableModule, @Input, @Output annotation classes, and the associated Spring @Configuration class that processes these annotations to create required channel beans and adapters automatically.

Create unit and integration tests for the new annotation model, validate that it works with existing module types, and ensure backward compatibility with modules that define channels explicitly as beans.

Complete any remaining Kryo serialization performance optimizations, validate that all optimized code paths work correctly with existing Spring XD payload types, and resolve any edge case serialization issues.

Create clear documentation for the Kryo optimization features, including configuration guidelines, performance benchmarks, best practices for custom payload types, and troubleshooting steps for common serialization issues.

Use existing AWS CloudFormation templates to provision the required EC2 instances, networking, and storage for running the Spring XD 1.2.x test suites, and configure security groups and access permissions.

activities.activity_name: Configure CI pipeline for 1.2.x on EC2
activities.activity_description: Update the Jenkins CI configuration to run the 1.2.x branch test suites on the newly provisioned EC2 infrastructure, configure test artifact storage on S3, and set up failure notifications.
Run a full test suite of the 1.2.x branch on the new EC2 infrastructure, resolve any environment-specific test failures, and confirm that the CI pipeline is stable and reliable.

Investigate existing Maven artifact resolution libraries (e.g., Aether) and patterns for installing modules to a running Spring XD runtime, evaluate tradeoffs of different approaches, and document the recommended implementation path.
Design the CLI command structure for specifying module Maven coordinates, the module download and installation workflow, and error handling for invalid or missing artifacts.

activities.activity_name: Refactor serialization codec to remove XD dependencies
activities.activity_description: Refactor the existing Spring XD serialization codec to remove all Spring XD specific dependencies, make it a standalone component that can be used in any Spring Integration project, and ensure all existing functionality is preserved.

activities.activity_name: Add codec tests to Spring Integration repo
activities.activity_description: Add comprehensive unit and integration tests for the refactored codec in the Spring Integration codebase, validate that it works with all supported serialization formats and payload types.

activities.activity_name: Update Spring XD to use SI codec dependency
activities.activity_description: Update the Spring XD pom.xml files to remove the local codec dependency and reference the new Spring Integration codec artifact, validate that all Spring XD functionality works correctly with the new dependency.

activities.activity_name: Review existing CloudController SPI spike deliverables
activities.activity_description: Review the existing spike deliverables for the CloudController XD Admin SPI (XD-3194 and XD-3229) to understand the implementation approach, identify gaps, and align with the existing spring-cloud-data and spring-cloud-stream module deployer code.

Implement the CloudController based XD Admin SPI using the ModuleLauncher interface, integrating with the existing spring-cloud-data module deployer code to support deploying data pipelines on Cloud Foundry.

activities.activity_name: Test CloudController SPI on Cloud Foundry
activities.activity_description: Create integration tests for the new SPI, deploy sample data pipelines to a test Cloud Foundry environment, validate that modules are launched correctly, and that pipeline functionality works as expected.
